criteria.semantics: A native <nav> landmark named by the nav's label (aria-label), its links in a native <ul>, one <li> each.

keyboard.outcome: Moves through the nav's links in order.

keyboard.key: Screen reader landmark keys (D, the rotor)
keyboard.outcome: Move to the nav by its name.

criteria.name: The nav's label.
criteria.role: Navigation landmark, and a list of its links.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the links grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the links stack or wrap, none cut off, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <nav> element.
The nav is named by its label in aria-label, so two navs on a page are told apart.
Its links are a native list: a <ul> with one <li> per link.
WHEN I list the landmarks with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR the nav by its name and the role of navigation.
WHEN I Tab into the nav I HEAR the list and how many links it has.

criteria.semantics: The nav's label, then its links, each a stop in the tab order; the nav itself is not. GPUI exposes no accessibility tree, so no navigation landmark reaches assistive technology.

keyboard.outcome: Moves through the nav's links in order.

criteria.name: The nav's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my system text size to 200% I SEE the label and the links grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I magnify the window with the system zoom I SEE the links whole.

check.statement: A nav adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE the nav's label above its links.
WHEN I reach the nav with a screen reader (VoiceOver, Orca, Narrator) I HEAR its name and the role of navigation.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit): every HEAR check fails on this face today. Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs), which no CI job runs yet (gpui/README.md, Verification); the rest are reported as not verified.
